what_worked: Data-transparency slide (5) surfacing uncategorized revenue as the biggest blind spot is genuinely useful framing.
fix_next: Rerun every calculation on the assigned 1,000-row frozen extract; the 8,782-row base invalidates nearly all claims.
verdict: Polished deck built on the wrong dataset; accuracy failures undermine otherwise competent storytelling.
factual_error_detail: Slide 1/2: claims 8,782 rows vs frozen 1,000. Slide 2: $15.4M MRR vs reference $15.6M total revenue (and conflates MRR with revenue). Slide 2: 57.2% zero-revenue vs reference 216/1000=21.6%. Slide 3: mean $1,752 not verifiable against 1,000-row set. Slide 4: AI count 1,430 vs reference 197; category totals all wrong. Slide 5: 3,264 uncategorized vs reference 274 missing. Slide 6: US 1,657 startups vs reference dataset scale. Slide 7: B2B/B2C counts (1,883/3,143) unverifiable against 1,000 rows. Slide 8: Stripe 59.4% of startups vs reference 636/1000=63.6%; Dodo 9.3% vs 50/1000=5%. Slide 8: Stripe 85.3% MRR vs reference 85.3% plausible but denominator wrong. Slide 10: correlation values drawn from wrong n. Slide 11: 1,952 for-sale vs 1,000-row cap.

evidence.insight: Slide 5 invisible-revenue observation and slide 10 correlation hierarchy (subs > DR > social) are decision-useful angles, but all underlying numbers are from a different dataset, so the insights cannot be trusted as stated.
evidence.narrative: Clear thesis ('top-heavy market') threaded from exec summary through distribution, categories, geography, payments, growth, drivers, acquisitions, and five takeaways. Logical arc with a purposeful landing slide. Bumped slightly from preliminary for coherent sequencing.
evidence.framing: Title slide names dataset and freeze date but claims 8,782 rows instead of 1,000. No limitations or missingness disclosure for the actual assigned dataset. Audience implied (builders/buyers) but never stated. Entire framing is built on wrong-scale data, leaving a cold reader unable to assess validity.
evidence.accuracy: Virtually every quantitative claim is derived from a larger (likely full-platform) dataset rather than the assigned 1,000-row frozen extract. Row count, revenue totals, category counts, zero-revenue share, provider splits, geography counts, and B2B/B2C figures all fail reference checks. At least 12 distinct factual mismatches identified.
evidence.visual: Consistent dark theme with teal/orange accents. Good hierarchy: section labels, big-number callouts, annotation boxes. Appropriate chart types (horizontal bar, donut, grouped bar, table). Slide 5 bar-chart axis labels slightly clipped. Professional but repetitive template feel across slides.
evidence.ai_slop: Uniform template layout across all 14 slides suggests automated generation. Phrases like 'brutally concentrated' and 'priced like a garage sale' are punchy but border on consulting-speak filler. The 8,782-row figure strongly suggests the student fed a full-platform scrape into an AI tool without verifying against the assigned 1,000-row extract.

change_reason: Raised narrative from 6.0 to 6.5 for genuinely coherent thesis threading and purposeful slide sequence; all other scores confirmed after independent review. Accuracy remains at 2.0 due to pervasive wrong-dataset errors.
